<reason>CON made the debate decidable: the motion either duplicates existing negligence/consumer/sector law on PRO’s documented “lethal dosage” parade case, or else it lacks a bounded spec and becomes hindsight liability. PRO’s user-as-deployer gap was real, but its own limiters (evals, contemporaneous practice) were turned into a diligence tax and a free first injury and never recovered. The clipped CON rebuttal is a real cost, not enough to offset the unanswered comparative frame.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: converting PRO’s “visible in evals / already used by prudent providers” answers into a tax on transparency and a rule that leaves the first victim of each new failure class uncompensated.</best_rebuttal>
